newsitem.title: ITALY: Fugitive 'Ndrangheta crime boss arrested in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive 'Ndrangheta crime boss arrested in Italy.

text.p: A fugitive Italian crime boss, one of the government's top 30 most-wanted criminals, was arrested in southern Italy on Tuesday after more than three years on the run, police said.
Giuseppe Mancuso, 48, was arrested in an early morning raid by some 50 police after authorities tracked him down to a friend's villa near Vibo Valentia, at the toe of the Italian peninsula.
Police had been searching for Mancuso, a leading boss of the 'Ndrangheta, the Calabrian version of the Sicilian Mafia, since 1993.
Mancuso was a member of the 'Ndrangheta's "Quintino", similar to the Sicilian Mafia's Cupola, or ruling body of bosses.

Magistrates in Calabria and the northern city of Milan had issued four warrants for his arrest on charges of murder, drugs trafficking and arms trafficking. Mancuso is suspected of having ordered five murders.
In a separate operation, police in Brindisi arrested 34 people suspected of links to the local Mafia in the south-eastern Puglia region.
Police confiscated nearly $10 million dollars in Italian lire in the raid, part of an investigation into money laundering.
